text:
sara_sales: Heads-up — Acme trial is hitting intermittent 5xxs during a ramp. Repro around ~120 rps from their load test. Demo in 30m, need a quick playbook and an immediate mitigation we can push.

mike_support: Which region/model are they hitting? Any example request_id or error payload? Can you paste a failed request/response?

sara_sales: Hitting us-east-1, model: open-llm-3b-q4 (hosted). Example from their tester: 
```
POST /v1/generate
{...}
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
content-type: application/json
x-rw-queue-depth: 48
{
  "error": "upstream overloaded, try again",
  "request_id": "req_0a9f3b2c"
}
```
Also seeing bursts of `HTTP 504` in the logs.

tom_sre: Looks like queue depth spike + autoscale lag. Our burstpool fallback probably didn't activate because min_replicas for that deployment is 0 and the coldstart for the fallback is ~45s. Quick mitigations: 
- flip the route to allow burstpool for this customer (temp)
- set min_replicas=2 for the model pool tied to this trial OR pin to a smaller model with warmer instances
- add a client-side ramp (token bucket) to smooth the initial push

Quick command to set fallback (I just ran this in staging):
```
redwoodctl routes update --customer acme --route default --allow-burst true --fallback-model open-llm-1b-q4
redwoodctl pool update open-llm-3b-q4 --min-replicas 2
```

mike_support: If you can't change infra in time, temporary toggle at the API layer: enable `failover_to_small_model=true` for their API key so requests get routed to the 1B variant when latency crosses threshold. That avoids a full autoscale cycle.

lucy_se: If we move them to reserved or bump min_replicas, what's the POC pricing delta? AE needs a number to tell Acme before the demo.

mike_support: Quick estimate: adding 2 min_replicas for the 3B pool in us-east-1 ~+$1200/day (ballpark, depends on spot vs on-demand). Fallback to 1B has negligible incremental cost during short bursts. I'll DM exact quoting.

sara_sales: I pushed `allow-burst=true` and updated route to fallback to `open-llm-1b-q4`. Rolling deploy started. Will monitor.

oncall-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0423-71 — "acme trial ramp: upstream overload" (link: https://internal.incidents/r/INC-2026-0423-71)

mike_support: Nice. While it's warming, can you grab a bundle of the proxy logs + the queue metrics around the spike? `curl -H "x-request-id: req_0a9f3b2c" https://logs.redwood.internal/bundle` should return what we need. Also include `redwoodctl metrics query --name queue_depth --since 15m --filter customer=acme`.

sara_sales: Uploaded logs to the incident and sent the bundle to the eng team. Errors dropped to single digits after the fallback route. Demo team notified.

tom_sre: Follow-up actions: 
- create a short runbook for AE trials: recommended min_replicas=1, warm fallback model prebind, and client ramp guidance (50rps per 30s).
- investigate why burstpool didn't auto-attach when queue_depth>40 (possible policy mismatch).
- consider reducing coldstart from 45s by pre-pulling kernels for common models.

lucy_se: I'll patch the POC pricing note and let Acme know the tradeoffs in the demo.

sara_sales: Thanks all, demo went ahead. Leaving this open for the follow-ups. :thumbsup:
